  "core_problem": "Clarification policy training on τ-bench now has one known prior: 'Asking to Clarify: Bridging Ambiguity in Tool-Agent-User Interactions' (OpenReview, 2025/2026) trains SFT, DPO, and GRPO for clarification on τ-bench via a dedicated Clarifier module—a separate component triggered after tool calls when key parameters are missing from fuzzy user requests. However, three precise gaps remain unaddressed by this and all other prior work. First, 'Asking to Clarify' uses fuzzy intent modeling on existing τ-bench data and does not construct an explicitly structured underspecified variant corpus; no work has applied the LHAW four-dimension taxonomy (arXiv:2602.10525) to τ-bench specifications, and the taxonomy's transferability (κ target ≥ 0.65) to airline/retail specifications is unvalidated. Second, no existing work trains a full joint policy end-to-end—as opposed to a dedicated trigger-conditioned Clarifier module—using GRPO on a structured, taxonomy-derived underspecified τ-bench variant corpus; the feasibility of producing measurable learning signal at N=30–50 variants is open. Third, no work compares a LHAW four-dimension dimension-aware secondary reward (binary LLM judge: does the clarification question target the labeled LHAW dimension?) against a scalar importance baseline (H/M/L, adapted from IntentionGym) within a τ-bench training setting. Critically, arXiv:2604.02869 (Apr 2026) establishes that naive per-turn dense rewards on τ-bench degrade performance by up to 14pp due to outcome advantage domination of per-turn signals, requiring Iterative Reward Calibration (IRC)—a rollout-discriminativeness-based calibration procedure using 5,952 rollouts in the original paper—before any secondary reward is applied; whether IRC-calibrated LHAW-dimension reward (using a smaller 600-episode feasibility-study corpus) produces distinguishable trends versus scalar importance is the third open question. UserRL (arXiv:2509.19736) never trained clarification directly on τ-bench (IntentionGym/IN3 is zero-shot evaluation only) and uses scalar H/M/L importance with no structured taxonomy. The four empirical questions addressable in 16 days: (1) Does LHAW taxonomy transfer to τ-bench specifications with κ ≥ 0.65? (2) Does full-policy MT-GRPO training on an explicitly constructed LHAW variant corpus (30–50 variants, hybrid discounted advantage with γ=0.9) produce measurable learning signal? (3) Does IRC-calibrated LHAW 4-dim secondary reward show distinguishable directional trends versus scalar importance? (4) Do trained policies zero-shot transfer to retail tasks?",
  "opportunity": "The compound feasibility gap that remains after 'Asking to Clarify'—and that no existing work addresses—has three components: (a) structured underspecification corpus construction (LHAW taxonomy transfer to τ-bench, validated by IAA); (b) full-policy GRPO clarification training on a taxonomy-derived variant corpus, as opposed to a dedicated Clarifier module operating on existing τ-bench data with fuzzy intent; (c) IRC-calibrated dimension-aware secondary reward, as opposed to goal-aware preference signals conditioned on ground-truth user requirements. 'Asking to Clarify' establishes that GRPO-based clarification training on τ-bench is feasible in principle, validating the episode structure. arXiv:2604.02869 establishes MT-GRPO with Iterative Reward Calibration as the correct multi-turn credit assignment mechanism for τ-bench and provides the hybrid discounted advantage formula A_{i,k}^{hybrid} = GN(Σ_{l=k}^{K-1} γ^{l-k} r_{i,l} + γ^{K-k} o_i) + λ·A_i^O (γ=0.9, λ=0.3); its IRC analysis used 5,952 rollouts on τ-bench airline. UserRL (arXiv:2509.19736) establishes Qwen3-32B as an effective local user simulator for τ-bench. τ³-bench provides 27 corrected airline and 26 corrected retail tasks as clean annotation targets. Together, these three prior works provide infrastructure for a 16-day feasibility study of full-policy clarification training with LHAW dimension-aware reward—a study that neither 'Asking to Clarify' (Clarifier module, fuzzy intent, no structured taxonomy) nor UserRL (general tool use, scalar importance, IntentionGym held out) nor arXiv:2604.02869 (general tool use, no clarification, no taxonomy) has conducted. The compound novel claim is: first feasibility evidence of full-policy MT-GRPO clarification training on a structured, LHAW-taxonomy-derived underspecified τ-bench variant corpus, with IRC-calibrated dimension-aware secondary reward calibrated from a 600-episode corpus (acknowledged as smaller than the 5,952-rollout IRC in arXiv:2604.02869; treated as a methodological limitation of the feasibility study scope). Days 1–3 (LHAW pilot, go/no-go gate); Days 3–7 (full annotation, 30–50 variants + IRC calibration corpus of 600 episodes running in parallel with annotation); Days 7–12 (MT-GRPO training, 2 conditions × 2 seeds, ~128 H100h); Days 12–14 (zero-shot retail evaluation); Days 14–16 (short paper). ARR May 25, 2026 deadline is exactly feasible.",
  "landscape": "**'Asking to Clarify: Bridging Ambiguity in Tool-Agent-User Interactions' (OpenReview, 2025/2026)** is the most critical prior work and directly challenges an earlier 'first GRPO on τ-bench' claim. This paper trains SFT, DPO, and GRPO for clarification on τ-bench (τ-airline domain) using a dedicated Clarifier module with three components: (1) Domain-Policy Tool Calling, (2) User-Driven Fuzzy Intent modeling for partially specified user goals, and (3) ReAsk Decision & Generation for targeted question generation. The Clarifier triggers after tool calls when key parameters are missing. It uses goal-aware preference signals conditioned on ground-truth user requirements. Architectural distinction from our work: 'Asking to Clarify' deploys a separate Clarifier sub-module triggered specifically after tool calls detect missing parameters, making clarification architecturally conditioned rather than an emergent joint behavior of a single policy. Our work is differentiated on four axes: (a) full-policy joint training (single Qwen3-8B policy decides tool calls, clarification questions, and responses from the same parameter set) vs. a trigger-conditioned Clarifier sub-module; (b) explicit underspecified variant corpus constructed via LHAW 4-dim taxonomy pipeline vs. fuzzy intent modeling on existing τ-bench data; (c) IRC-calibrated LHAW dimension-aware binary-judge reward vs. goal-aware preference signals; and (d) zero-shot cross-domain evaluation (airline→retail) not reported by 'Asking to Clarify'.

**UserRL (arXiv:2509.19736, Sep 2025)** is the second most critical prior. Its five training gyms include TauGym (τ-bench, general tool use) but IntentionGym—which uses IN3 (Qian et al., ACL 2024) and rewards agents for uncovering missing intent details at scalar H/M/L importance levels—is held out as zero-shot evaluation. UserRL never trains clarification on τ-bench, never applies a structured underspecification taxonomy, and validates Qwen3-32B as an effective local user simulator.

**MT-GRPO + Iterative Reward Calibration on τ-bench (arXiv:2604.02869, Apr 2026)** establishes the correct multi-turn credit assignment mechanism for τ-bench. The paper uses a hybrid discounted advantage: A_{i,k}^{hybrid} = GN(Σ_{l=k}^{K-1} γ^{l-k} r_{i,l} + γ^{K-k} o_i) + λ·A_i^O, where γ=0.9 is the step-level discount factor, λ=0.3 weights the undiscounted outcome signal, and GN is group normalization across rollouts at each turn position k. The IRC analysis used 5,952 rollouts for τ-bench airline. The paper's key finding is that naive dense per-turn rewards degrade performance by up to 14pp because outcome advantages (|A^O| ≈ 0.87) overwhelm per-turn signals (|A^I| ≈ 0.05), reversing intended training signals. IRC addresses this by computing point-biserial correlations between per-turn reward tier presence and binary task success, then setting reward weights proportional to discriminative power. Training used 8 H20 GPUs (96GB each) with Megatron-Core and batch size 8. Applied to τ-bench airline: Qwen3-30B-A3B improves from 58.0% to 69.5% (+11.5pp). This paper is general tool use, NOT clarification, and uses NO underspecification taxonomy.

**MUA-RL (arXiv:2508.18669, Aug 2025)** integrates LLM-simulated users into GRPO for general multi-turn tool use on τ²-bench (45.4% on TAU2 Airline with 32B); treats neither underspecification nor clarification gating as first-class problems.

**SpeakRL (arXiv:2512.13159, Dec 2025)** trains clarification question-asking via RL (+20.14% task completion) on the synthetic SpeakER dialogue dataset—not a live tool-use benchmark.

**CLARITI (arXiv:2604.14624, Apr 2026)** trains an 8B clarification module on SWE tasks using multi-stage GRPO with Shapley-attributed proxy rewards; SWE episode intractability validates τ-bench's auto-verifiable structure.

**GRPO-CR (arXiv:2601.16400, Jan 2026)** applies GRPO to VQA clarification (+0.156 F1) demonstrating GRPO's effectiveness for clarification on non-tool-use benchmarks.

**Reward-Weighted Clarification Fine-Tuning (arXiv:2506.06964, NeurIPS 2025)** applies offline RL to short-horizon QA agents—no auto-verifiable episode reward, offline setting, no structured taxonomy.

**Ask or Assume? (arXiv:2603.26233, Mar 2026)** achieves 69.4% on underspecified SWE-bench via multi-agent scaffold (OpenHands + Claude Sonnet 4.5)—no RL, no τ-bench.

**ClarEval (arXiv:2603.00187, Feb/Mar 2026)** proposes ATC/KQC metrics for clarification in coding agents—no RL, no τ-bench.

**Turn-Level Reward Design (arXiv:2505.11821, May 2026)** extends GRPO and PPO to multi-turn variants enabling fine-grained credit assignment; complements MT-GRPO but tested on QA datasets, not τ-bench.

**LHAW (arXiv:2602.10525)** provides a validated dataset-agnostic taxonomy (Goals, Constraints, Inputs, Context) with empirical agent-trial classification across TheAgentCompany, SWE-Bench Pro, and MCP-Atlas—not τ-bench.

**τ-bench SOTA (BenchLM leaderboard, May 2026):** MiMo-V2.5-Pro at 72.9%, Qwen3.6 Plus at 70.7%. 8B fine-tuned models on clarification-requiring variants remain well below frontier.",
  "approach": "This is a 16-day proof-of-concept feasibility study targeting EMNLP 2026 Findings (short paper, 4+1 pages, ARR May 25, 2026 submission). The novelty claim is precisely scoped: first feasibility evidence of full-policy MT-GRPO clarification training on a structured, LHAW-taxonomy-derived underspecified τ-bench variant corpus, with IRC-calibrated dimension-aware secondary reward. This is distinct from 'Asking to Clarify' (dedicated Clarifier module + fuzzy intent + goal-aware preference) and from arXiv:2604.02869 (general tool use + no taxonomy). All claims are explicitly pre-registered as 'proof-of-concept; N=30–50 variants; minimum detectable effect ≥15pp at p<0.1 with 2 seeds; results below this threshold reported as exploratory trends only.'

**Days 1–3: LHAW Taxonomy Transfer Pilot (go/no-go gate)**
Apply LHAW Phase 1 (LLM-based segment extraction) to 5 τ³ airline tasks (3 corrected, 2 uncorrected), mapping each specification element to Goal/Constraint/Input/Context. Known challenge cases pre-resolved: fare-waiver quantity restrictions → Constraint; waiver outcome → Goal; numeric seat IDs → Input; cabin-class defaults → Context. Two researchers independently label; compute Cohen's κ. Go decision requires κ ≥ 0.65 and all four dimensions present in ≥2 of 5 tasks.

*Borderline κ procedure (pre-registered)*: If 0.60 ≤ κ < 0.65 after one definition-refinement pass, annotate 5 additional tasks (N=10 total), use pooled κ as the final gate. If κ still < 0.65 on N=10, declare feasibility blocker and abort—this constitutes Option B (FAIL), which is itself publishable as a negative taxonomy-transfer finding. A κ below 0.60 after first pass aborts immediately (hard threshold). Cost: ~$1–2 API, 2 person-days.

**Days 3–7: Annotation + IRC Calibration Corpus**
Contingent on pilot go decision. These two sub-tasks run in parallel.

(a) *LHAW annotation*: Apply full two-phase LHAW pipeline (segment extraction + outcome-criticality labeling) to all 5 pilot tasks, generating ~6–10 variants per task (30–50 total). Add scalar importance labels (H/M/L adapted from IntentionGym) in parallel for baseline. 25% manual QC spot-check. ~$3–8 annotation API cost. Conducted primarily during daytime (Days 3–7).

(b) *IRC calibration corpus*: Generate 600 rollout episodes from the base Qwen3-8B policy on the 30–50 variants (without LHAW-dim secondary reward active), running as a background overnight process beginning Day 3. At expected Qwen3-8B success rates of 20–30% on clarification-requiring variants, 600 episodes yields ~150–180 successes distributed approximately uniformly across 4 LHAW dimensions (~37–45 per dimension). This exceeds the n>25 positive-instance threshold required for approximate normality of point-biserial correlation estimates (standard reliability threshold for this statistic). We explicitly acknowledge this corpus is substantially smaller than the 5,952 rollouts used for IRC analysis in arXiv:2604.02869; this is a methodological limitation of the feasibility study scope, stated as such in the paper. Wall-clock: ~18 hours at 40% GPU utilization (IRC runs inference-only; no backprop), completing within the Days 3–7 window. IRC analysis (point-biserial correlation between clarification-turn presence and binary task success per LHAW dimension) and reward weight calibration are performed Days 6–7. Expected: one or two LHAW dimension categories may have near-zero discriminative correlation; those receive zero secondary reward weight in the calibrated condition. Near-zero correlation for all four dimensions would collapse Condition A to Condition B—itself a reportable finding ('IRC finds LHAW-dim reward non-discriminable from scalar at N=600 feasibility corpus').

**Days 7–12: MT-GRPO Training on 2×H100 SXM**

*Architectural distinction from 'Asking to Clarify' (one-sentence operationalization)*: In this paper, Qwen3-8B is a single joint policy that decides—at any turn—whether to invoke API tools, ask a clarifying question, or produce a final response; all action types are sampled from the same parameter set without an explicit trigger condition. In contrast, 'Asking to Clarify' deploys a separate Clarifier sub-module activated only after tool calls detect missing parameters, making clarification architecturally conditioned rather than an emergent behavior of a unified policy.

*Memory management — interleaved rollout/update schedule*: Full FP32 Adam fine-tuning of Qwen3-8B requires approximately 96GB excluding activations: 16GB BF16 model weights (8B × 2 bytes) + 64GB FP32 Adam optimizer states (8B × 4 bytes × 2 for first and second moment vectors) + 16GB BF16 gradients. Co-locating this with the Qwen3-32B simulator (64GB, TP=2) and Qwen3-8B judge (16GB) simultaneously would require ~176GB, exceeding the 160GB available. We therefore use a phase-separated interleaved rollout/update schedule:
- *Rollout phase*: load policy for BF16 forward-only inference (16GB) + Qwen3-32B simulator (TP=2 across both GPUs, 64GB) + Qwen3-8B judge (16GB) = 96GB peak VRAM; FP32 Adam states are not loaded during rollout.
- *Update phase*: unload simulator and judge; load policy with FP32 Adam states and BF16 gradients (96GB) + gradient-checkpointed activations (batch size 16, ~500-token average sequences: ~4–8GB with gradient checkpointing enabled) = ~100–104GB peak VRAM.
NVLink between the two H100 SXM GPUs enables fast model swapping between phases (~15–30 seconds per phase transition). Peak VRAM in both phases: ≤104GB, well within 160GB. NVLink verification and phase-swap latency benchmarking are budgeted into the Day 7–8 infrastructure slot.

*Multi-turn credit assignment*: We adopt the hybrid discounted advantage formulation from arXiv:2604.02869 verbatim: A_{i,k}^{hybrid} = GN(Σ_{l=k}^{K-1} γ^{l-k} r_{i,l} + γ^{K-k} o_i) + λ·A_i^O, where γ=0.9 is the step-level discount factor (early turns receive discounted future intermediate rewards), λ=0.3 weights the undiscounted outcome advantage added outside group normalization, o_i is the binary task-success outcome reward, r_{i,l} is the per-turn intermediate reward at turn l, and GN denotes group normalization across G=4 rollouts at each turn position k. The γ=0.9 discount ensures early-turn gradients reflect discounted future returns rather than uniform credit; the separate λ·A^O term prevents outcome information from being fully absorbed into the discounted sum and becoming unrecoverable after GN. This differs from a simplified undiscounted sum (as in earlier versions of this proposal) and matches the validated τ-bench implementation. We reproduce the formula in the paper's methodology section with attribution. Justification for MT-GRPO over GTPO (arXiv:2511.14846): GTPO's self-supervised reward shaping is designed for code/math tasks; MT-GRPO with this hybrid advantage has been validated directly on τ-bench airline (arXiv:2604.02869).

*Pre-training outcome variance check (before committing training compute)*: On 20 held-out episodes from the 30–50 training variants, compute per-group success rate across G=4 rollouts for each variant. Training proceeds only if the mean per-group success rate falls in [0.10, 0.90]. If mean success rate < 0.10 (near-zero clarification quality; advantages uniformly negative; minimal gradient signal), increase decoding temperature incrementally (T: 0.7 → 0.8 → 1.0 → 1.2) until criterion is met. If mean success rate > 0.90 (base policy already solves variants; near-zero advantage variance), add additional underspecification to the lowest-complexity variants or increase user simulator intent ambiguity. This check takes ~30 minutes and prevents wasting 15–16 hours of H100 time on a degenerate training run.

Two training conditions (each run with 2 random seeds, sequential runs):
- Condition A (LHAW-dim, IRC-calibrated): r_combined = r_task + w_dim × r_dim, where w_dim is determined by IRC analysis (target |w_dim × A^I| ≈ 0.3 × |A^O| to maintain positive advantage direction consistent with the λ=0.3 calibration in arXiv:2604.02869); r_dim is binary judge: does question target the labeled LHAW dimension?
- Condition B (scalar): r_combined = r_task + 0.3 × r_scalar (importance level H=1.0/M=0.67/L=0.33, normalized; weight 0.3 kept fixed, not IRC-calibrated, for clean comparison of reward structure rather than weight tuning)

*Condition comparison scope (pre-registered limitation)*: Condition A and Condition B differ simultaneously on reward structure (4-dim binary vs. H/M/L scalar) and weight calibration method (IRC-derived vs. fixed 0.3). The comparison tests the joint effect of dimension-aware structure and IRC calibration, not dimension-awareness in isolation. A fully controlled comparison would require a third condition (IRC-calibrated scalar); this is deferred to the fully-powered follow-up study.

Hyperparameters: G=4 rollouts per prompt, 5 epochs, batch size 16. Anti-hacking constraints: BLEU-1 overlap with prior rollout questions < 0.6; minimum 10-word filter; interrogative marker required.

*Revised wall-clock per run*: 40 variants × 4 rollouts × 5 epochs × 15 user_turns (median of 10–30 total turns per episode) = 12,000 Qwen3-32B simulator inference calls. At ~3 seconds per call on TP=2, raw compute = 36,000s. At 65% GPU utilization (idle during τ-bench episode bookkeeping between turns, per arXiv:2604.02869 observation): ~15–16 hours wall-clock per run. Per run H100h: 16 hours × 2 GPUs = 32 H100h. Four runs total: ~128 H100h for training.

*Run schedule*: Condition A seed 1 (Day 7–8); IRC calibration analysis + Condition A seed 2 (Day 8–9); Condition B seed 1 (Day 9–10); Condition B seed 2 (Day 10–11); evaluation and buffer (Day 11–12).

**Days 12–14: Zero-Shot Evaluation on 5 Retail Tasks**
Select 5 corrected τ³ retail tasks. Evaluate: (1) prompt-only Qwen3-8B baseline; (2) GRPO task-success reward only (no secondary reward); (3) Condition A (LHAW-dim, IRC-calibrated); (4) Condition B (scalar). 5 evaluation trials × 5 tasks × 2 seeds = 50 episodes per condition. Report task success rate with bootstrapped 95% CI across 2 seeds. Explicit power statement pre-registered: 'N=50 episodes per condition; minimum detectable effect ≥15pp at p<0.1 under 2 seeds; results below this threshold reported as exploratory trends only.' Evaluation GPU cost: ~5 H100h.

**Days 14–16: Short Paper Writing (4+1 pages, EMNLP Findings)**
Pre-assigned section space budget to ensure 4 ACL-format pages are sufficient:
- Introduction (0.5 pages): problem, gap vs. 'Asking to Clarify' and arXiv:2604.02869, three contributions
- Related Work (0.5 pages): condensed 6-entry table format covering 'Asking to Clarify', UserRL, arXiv:2604.02869, CLARITI, SpeakRL, LHAW
- Background & Setup (0.4 pages): τ³-bench, LHAW taxonomy, MT-GRPO hybrid advantage formula (A_{i,k}^{hybrid} = GN(Σ γ^{l-k} r_{i,l} + γ^{K-k} o_i) + λ·A^O_i, γ=0.9, λ=0.3), Qwen3-32B simulator
- Methodology (0.9 pages): LHAW pilot + IAA result (0.2p), variant construction + 600-episode IRC calibration corpus (0.3p), interleaved memory schedule + MT-GRPO training conditions (0.4p)
- Results (1.4 pages): training curves [1 compact figure, 0.5p], zero-shot retail table [1 table, 0.4p], uncertainty + power statement (0.3p), negative-result framing if flat (0.2p)
- Limitations & Conclusion (0.3 pages): includes (1) condition comparison confound (Condition A vs. B tests joint effect of reward structure and calibration method, not dimension-awareness alone; fully controlled comparison deferred to powered follow-up); (2) IRC corpus size (600 episodes vs. 5,952 in arXiv:2604.02869; correlation estimates have wider CIs at this scale); (3) N=2 seeds; (4) N=5 retail tasks for zero-shot evaluation.

Three reportable findings: (1) IAA κ value—establishes LHAW transferability to τ-bench, citable independent of training outcome; (2) training curves—binary feasibility finding: does MT-GRPO produce reward signal on 30–50 LHAW clarification variants?; (3) zero-shot retail evaluation—directional comparison with uncertainty quantification. Paper framing: 'We provide first feasibility evidence that full-policy MT-GRPO clarification training on an LHAW-taxonomy-derived underspecified τ-bench variant corpus produces measurable learning signal, that LHAW four-dimension taxonomy transfers with κ=X.XX, and that IRC-calibrated dimension-aware reward shows [directional trend] versus scalar importance baseline—warranting a fully-powered follow-up.' Flat training curves or failed taxonomy transfer are reported as negative feasibility results—publishable given the first-ever nature of the experiment.",

# Paper Summary: When and What to Ask

**Title:** "When and What to Ask: AskBench and Rubric-Guided RLVR for LLM Clarification"

**Abstract Overview:**
The research addresses a critical limitation where "LLMs often respond even when prompts omit critical details or include misleading information, leading to hallucinations." The authors investigate methods to evaluate and improve LLMs' ability to recognize when clarification is needed.

**Benchmark Settings:**

- **AskMind:** Covers intent-deficient queries requiring clarification
- **AskOverconfidence:** Addresses queries containing false premises that must be identified and corrected

**Method Overview - AskBench:**
The benchmark converts standard QA pairs into multi-turn interactions with explicit checkpoints. A unified judge loop evaluates final answers and simulates user responses.

**Reward Mechanism:**
The paper proposes "rubric-guided reinforcement learning with verifier-based rewards (RLVR), which uses structured rubrics to encourage targeted clarification." This approach uses verifier-based reward signals aligned with evaluation rubrics.

**Results:**
Experiments demonstrated "consistent improvements in accuracy, rubric adherence, and interaction efficiency, with strong generalization to unseen domains."

*Memory management — interleaved rollout/update schedule*: Full FP32 Adam fine-tuning of Qwen3-8B requires approximately 96GB excluding activations: 16GB BF16 model weights (8B × 2 bytes) + 64GB FP32 Adam optimizer states (8B × 4 bytes × 2 for first and second moment vectors) + 16GB BF16 gradients. Co-locating this with the Qwen3-32B simulator (64GB, TP=2) and Qwen3-8B judge (16GB) simultaneously would require ~176GB, exceeding the 160GB available. We therefore use a phase-separated interleaved rollout/update schedule:
- *Rollout phase*: load policy for BF16 forward-only inference (16GB) + Qwen3-32B simulator (TP=2 across both GPUs, 64GB) + Qwen3-8B judge (16GB) = 96GB peak VRAM; FP32 Adam states are not loaded during rollout.
- *Update phase*: unload simulator and judge; load policy with FP32 Adam states and BF16 gradients (96GB) + gradient-checkpointed activations (batch size 16, ~500-token average sequences: ~4–8GB with gradient checkpointing enabled) = ~100–104GB peak VRAM.
NVLink between the two H100 SXM GPUs enables fast model swapping between phases (~15–30 seconds per phase transition). Peak VRAM in both phases: ≤104GB, well within 160GB. NVLink verification and phase-swap latency benchmarking are budgeted into the Day 7–8 infrastructure slot.

*Multi-turn credit assignment*: We adopt the hybrid discounted advantage formulation from arXiv:2604.02869 verbatim: A_{i,k}^{hybrid} = GN(Σ_{l=k}^{K-1} γ^{l-k} r_{i,l} + γ^{K-k} o_i) + λ·A_i^O, where γ=0.9 is the step-level discount factor (early turns receive discounted future intermediate rewards), λ=0.3 weights the undiscounted outcome advantage added outside group normalization, o_i is the binary task-success outcome reward, r_{i,l} is the per-turn intermediate reward at turn l, and GN denotes group normalization across G=4 rollouts at each turn position k. The γ=0.9 discount ensures early-turn gradients reflect discounted future returns rather than uniform credit; the separate λ·A^O term prevents outcome information from being fully absorbed into the discounted sum and becoming unrecoverable after GN. This differs from a simplified undiscounted sum (as in earlier versions of this proposal) and matches the validated τ-bench implementation. We reproduce the formula in the paper's methodology section with attribution. Justification for MT-GRPO over GTPO (arXiv:2511.14846): GTPO's self-supervised reward shaping is designed for code/math tasks; MT-GRPO with this hybrid advantage has been validated directly on τ-bench airline (arXiv:2604.02869).

*Pre-training outcome variance check (before committing training compute)*: On 20 held-out episodes from the 30–50 training variants, compute per-group success rate across G=4 rollouts for each variant. Training proceeds only if the mean per-group success rate falls in [0.10, 0.90].
